mainEntity.name: Will a veneer hide a cracked tooth completely?

acceptedAnswer.text: A veneer covers the front-facing surface of a tooth and can mask the visual appearance of surface-level craze lines effectively. However, a veneer does not repair the underlying tooth structure. If the crack extends deeper than the enamel, covering it cosmetically without addressing the structural issue first would not be appropriate. Your dentist will assess whether the tooth is clinically stable and suitable for veneer placement during an examination.

mainEntity.name: Can a small crack in a tooth get worse over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in some cases it can. A crack that begins as a minor surface imperfection may, over time and under the repeated pressures of biting, chewing, and temperature changes, propagate further into the tooth. This is why monitoring existing cracks through regular dental check-ups is recommended. Early identification allows for timely intervention, which may enable a more straightforward approach to treatment in many cases.

mainEntity.name: How does a dentist assess whether a crack is serious?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental professionals use several methods to evaluate cracks. Visual examination under good lighting is a starting point. Transillumination — shining a light through the tooth — can help reveal the extent of a fracture. Bite tests (asking the patient to bite on a small object) can help localise the location of a crack. Dental probing around the gum line may detect fractures extending towards the root. Dental X-rays may also be used, although hairline fractures are not always visible on standard radiographs.

mainEntity.name: Is there any pain associated with craze lines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Craze lines — the most superficial type of enamel crack — typically do not cause pain or sensitivity. Because they do not reach the dentine or deeper layers, the nerve tissue of the tooth is unaffected. If you do experience discomfort or sensitivity alongside what appears to be a crack, this may suggest the fracture is more than superficial, and a dental assessment would be advisable.

mainEntity.name: Are veneers a permanent solution for cracked teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Veneers are a long-term cosmetic restoration, but they are not considered permanent in the way that the natural tooth structure is. Porcelain veneers typically have a lifespan of many years when well maintained, but they can chip, debond, or require replacement over time. Importantly, veneers do not prevent an underlying crack from progressing if the cause of the cracking (such as tooth grinding) is not also addressed. Ongoing maintenance and regular dental review remain important after veneer placement.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a cracked tooth is left untreated?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends greatly on the type and severity of the crack. Superficial craze lines may remain stable for many years without any intervention required. However, structural cracks — particularly those reaching the dentine or pulp — may progress if left unaddressed, potentially leading to sensitivity, pain, or infection. In more advanced cases, the long-term viability of the tooth may be affected. Early professional assessment provides the best opportunity for straightforward and effective management.
